s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital swelling with vision deterioration and proptosis
salient_findings: Left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
Progressive deterioration of vision in the left eye
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Left fronto-orbital swelling for 10 years
Progressive vision deterioration in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis became more pronounced over the past month
Left globe displaced inferiorly and medially
No history of endocrine abnormalities
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT
Involvement of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing

shortlist.label: Orbital meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and involvement of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing are consistent with meningioma

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit is consistent with fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Sphenoid wing meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the sphenoid wing and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof are consistent with sphenoid wing meningioma

shortlist.label: Orbital osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing could be consistent with osteoma

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the orbital roof and sphenoid wing, and expansive lytic bony lesion are consistent with chordoma

raw.rationale: The involvement of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing, along with the heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI, is most consistent with a sphenoid wing meningioma, which is known to cause such bony changes and orbital displacement.

rejected.label: Orbital meningioma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific involvement of the sphenoid wing and the pattern of bony lesions is more characteristic of sphenoid wing meningioma.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia could explain the lytic bony lesions, but it does not typically cause a heterogeneous enhancing mass as seen on MRI.

rejected.label: Orbital osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is a benign bone tumor that does not typically cause progressive vision deterioration or the extensive bony involvement seen in this case.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordoma is a rare tumor that could involve the sphenoid region, but it is less likely given the specific pattern of orbital and bony involvement described.
